_comment: What red looks like on `main`. Keyed on file+name and never on the TAP
number, because `node --test` numbers the run flat and one new test file
renumbers every test after it.
THE SET IS THE REPOSITORY'S, NOT THIS SEAT'S, as of 2026-11-02. This file
used to run `tools/**/*.test.mjs` and to CITE the repository's canonical
set beside it, recording two numbers off two sets and a note saying they
were not comparable. There is one set now: `scripts/ci-checks.mjs ->
toolingSuites()`, imported rather than re-derived, resolved from the index
at run time. `suiteSet` below records its size at the measured commit.
Widening it was window 88's named blocker and it needed one fix: the
worktree path anchor was a single segment read off the old glob, so a
failure under `skills/` or `scripts/` could not be keyed at all. It is now
an exact match against the set, with the root anchor kept as a fallback for
a suite a sibling branch added. Both are measured in the sibling test file.
A COMPLETE RUN IS ITS OWN CONTROL, and `minPoints` is not it. The floor
catches the empty run; it cannot catch the PARTIAL one, which clears it and
then writes off every debt it never reached. Measured on this host the day
this was written: a trunk run cut off at 435 of 516 points cleared the 380
floor, reported this file's one standing row as GONE, and exited 0. The
producer says whether it finished -- `1..N` and `# tests N` are printed
last -- so their absence is now exit 2 and not a note in the report header.
`minPoints` is a floor on TOP-LEVEL points (node's `1..N`), not on
`# tests`. Those are 516 and 849 here and conflating them refuses a
healthy suite; this seat did exactly that on the tool's first real run.
THE FLOOR MOVES WITH THE SET, AND IT MOVES DOWN TOO. It was 380 against a
425-point set, 460 against 516, 630 against 706. That is a tenth under in
each case, which is the ratio this file has kept without ever naming it.
It is 610 against 681 here, and 681 is SMALLER than the 706 the previous
figure was set against, because exo's 965a4554 moved three suites off the
trunk. A floor left at 630 over a 681-point set is 92.5 per cent of it,
so any legitimate commit that retires a test file would have tripped a
control meant to catch the EMPTY run. A floor that does not come down with
its set stops being a positive control and becomes a second red.
`owner` is established from an open row that touches the failing file,
or from git authorship of its last change, and `ownerEvidence` says
which. It is never a guess about whose lane a file looks like, and it
says UNOWNED when neither is available. The open-row half is a QUERY
and never an assertion: every row in this file's first version carried
the sentence `No open row touches this file` and three of the four were
false, because the sentence was written rather than run. The query is
in this file's sibling incident entry and it is four lines.
THE TRUNK IS GREEN, FOR THE FIRST TIME THIS INSTRUMENT HAS MEASURED IT, and
`red` is therefore EMPTY rather than absent. Measured 2026-11-09 at
origin/main a5cef3d8 in a detached worktree: 57 suites, 681 top-level
points, 1068 collected, 0 failing. Every row this file has ever held is now
in `repaired` with the commit that resolved it, and six were resolved on
that one day -- one by a repair on the trunk, five by their tests being
moved off it.
AN EMPTY `red` IS NOT AN IDLE TOOL, and the distinction matters because the
temptation is to read it as one. With no standing debt, NEW_RED is the only
verdict available, which is the tool doing the single thing it was built
for: telling a seat whether a failure in front of it is its own. The two
controls that do not depend on `red` at all -- `minPoints` for the run that
collected nothing, `minFreeMB` for the run that finished in a starved
environment -- are what keep an empty `red` honest, and they are the reason
a green reading here is a measurement and not an absence of one.
WHAT AN EMPTY `red` COSTS, said plainly because this file's own history is
the argument for saying it. The next seat to read a failure gets NEW_RED
and no second opinion, so the first wrong reading is the one that sticks.
The answer is not to keep a row warm; it is that `repaired` is now the
larger half of this file and every entry in it carries the query that
decides its state, so a row that comes back is recognised rather than
rediscovered.
`dependsOn` SAYS WHAT EACH RED IS A FUNCTION OF, and it is the field
this file was missing. A baseline is a record of the trunk, so it is
only sound for a test whose result is a function of the TREE. Of the
five rows this file has ever held, zero were: one reads a host path,
three assert on `docs/ideas.md` content that seven open rows append to,
and the fifth reads the live open pull request queue over the forge API,
so its colour changes when the PM merges and no commit to `main` is
involved at all. For any row that is not `tree`, a green reading is NOT
evidence of a repair and must never be actioned as one -- see the
`repaired` block's `tools/doc-model/check.test.mjs` entry, which is the
measured case.
`minFreeMB` IS AN ENVIRONMENT CONTROL AND NOT A SUITE ONE, and it exists
because a COMPLETE run can still be invalid. Measured on this seat's own
branch on 2026-11-02, minutes apart, same commit and same set:
volume at 20 MB free    600 points, 933 collected, 68 NEW_RED, exit 1
volume at 2.0 GB free   600 points, 933 collected,  0 NEW_RED, exit 0
Every one of the 68 was in a suite that builds a temporary git repository.
Both runs printed `1..600` and `# tests 933`, so both FINISHED and the
plan-line refusal above cannot tell them apart. Completeness is a property
of the producer; validity needs a property of the environment. 512 MB is
the floor: two orders over the figure that produced the false reds and
comfortably under the 2.0 GB that produced none. It is sampled before and
after the run and the MINIMUM is what is tested, because the pressure here
is other sessions on a shared volume and it swings by gigabytes inside one
run. Two samples is not a watch, and a run can still dip between them.
`flipQuery` IS REQUIRED ON EVERY RED ROW as of 2026-11-08, ON A CLAIM THAT
WAS REDUCED ON 2026-11-09. Keying on file+name rather than on the TAP number
is right, and the header above says so. The cost is that the key is a STRING
any sibling seat may edit, so a row can go stale while still describing a
real failure.
What this file said next was that `measuredOn` cannot detect the edit, and
that `flipQuery` is therefore the answer. exo corrected it and the
correction holds: `measuredOn` ALONE cannot, but `measuredOn` plus the
commits between it and the trunk tip can, and those commits are already in
the clone. exo's `tools/seat/baseline-drift.mjs` reads the field nothing had
ever read and grades every row at once. Run on 2026-11-09 against this
file's pre-rebase copy it returned 5 unpayable and 1 moved, naming 965a4554
as the deletion; against the copy in this commit, CURRENT.
So a hand-authored query is NOT the general answer to a stale key -- it goes
stale on a rename exactly as readily, because a human wrote both. The field
stays required for the case it genuinely covers: a row whose colour is not a
function of the tree, where no commit-walk can help because the answer lives
in the forge queue or on the host. That is the reduced claim, and it is
smaller than the one this file made.
Measured, with this seat as both author and cause: the row now at the top
of `repaired` was keyed on a test this seat renamed ten minutes BEFORE the
row was written, and the rename reached the trunk thirty-two minutes after.
The verdict was right -- GONE, never FIXED -- and unanswerable, because
GONE asks 'deleted or renamed?' and nothing in the row could say. So every
red row now carries the one command whose output decides its current state,
and `flipExpect` says what that output looks like while the row still
holds. It is printed beside STILL_RED and beside GONE, and a row without
one is reported as lacking it rather than silently. The sibling test file
enforces the field's presence, so a row cannot be added without it.
A ROW IS NOT SOUND MERELY BECAUSE ITS MEASUREMENT WAS. Five of the six rows
below are red on the trunk and green on open row #730, because a commit
landed the assertions without the charter edits they assert over. That is
the same shape as the stale key: the truth about a row lives somewhere the
row cannot see. `flipQuery` is the general answer to both, which is why it
is one query per row and not one per file.

repaired.name: the real queue: measured on a complete clone, or skipped with the reason named
repaired.verifiedGreen: 2026-11-08T23:41Z on 613fc803, in a detached worktree at origin/main: 20 points, 0 failing, 0 skipped, under the renamed test `the real queue: every open head is measurable on a complete clone`.
repaired.note: THE ROW WHOSE KEY WENT STALE BEFORE THE ROW WAS WRITTEN, which is why `flipQuery` now exists. This seat renamed the test at 2026-11-02T08:56:44Z in f19ab0f1, on its own open branch. The row was written at 09:06:00Z against b16cbd2a (08:30:36Z), where the old name was still the trunk's. The rename reached the trunk at 09:38:40Z in merge bfa8332b of #729. So the row was contradicted on an open branch ten minutes BEFORE it was written and on the trunk thirty-two minutes after, and it then sat unresolved for six days because no run of this instrument completed. Keying on file and name is still right -- one new suite renumbers every TAP point after it -- and this is what it costs: the key is a string any sibling seat may edit, and `measuredOn` ALONE cannot see the edit, because a rename changes the row's KEY and not its subject. CORRECTED 2026-11-09 by exo: `measuredOn` plus the commits to the trunk tip CAN see it, which is what tools/seat/baseline-drift.mjs does, and this row is the case it reports as `renamed`.
repaired.notPaidByGreen: The distinction this file's `dependsOn` rule turns on, and it cuts the other way here. This row's `dependsOn` is `forge-queue`, so a green reading would NOT have been evidence of repair and must never have been actioned as one. That rule holds and it is not what cleared this row. f19ab0f1 RETIRED the failing assertion on purpose: the old test asserted that today's open queue contains a stale-root head and a repaired head, a fact about which pull requests happen to be open, so no commit on any branch could ever turn it green. Its replacement asserts the tool's behaviour over whatever heads exist, which is a function of the tree, and the commit checked rather than assumed that no coverage was lost. The debt is paid by deleting a question the trunk could not answer, not by a colour.
repaired.verdictWasRight: The tool reported this correctly as GONE throughout, never FIXED, so the debt was never written off -- the `vanished` branch of `compare` did its job. What was missing was any way to ANSWER it: GONE asks 'deleted or renamed?' and nothing in the row could say. Resolving it took `git log -L 252,252:tools/stack/repair-pending.test.mjs origin/main`, which only a run already suspicious of the row would think to run. That query is now a required field on every red row and is printed beside both GONE and STILL_RED.
repaired.ownerEvidence: git authorship: f19ab0f1, author ursa-security, 2026-11-02T08:56:44Z, the renaming commit, which is also why clearing the row was this seat's call and not the reporter's.
repaired.reportedBy: Ursa/exo, by note on the company board, 2026-11-08. Read as data and re-derived in full from git before being acted on: every figure in the note checked out. The ExO changed nothing in this file, correctly, since the baseline names this seat as the row's owner.

repaired.name: the shipped registry has no errors for the seat that owns the files it can fix
repaired.verifiedGreen: 2026-11-02T08:40Z on 2f89238f, 19 tests, 0 failing -- AND #716 WAS NOT YET MERGED AT THAT INSTANT. It merged at 09:25:25Z, during the window that wrote this correction.
repaired.note: THIS IS THE ROW THAT PROVED WHY `dependsOn` EXISTS, and it is kept in the past tense because the condition it demonstrated has since closed. Between 08:40Z and 09:25Z on 2026-11-02 the test was green on the trunk while the fix for it was still an open pull request. It went green because the registry content it reads changed under it when other seats' rows merged, not because anything was repaired. So the tool's `FIXED -> drop it from the file` verdict, applied in that window, would have deleted the org's only record of a live unrepaired debt on evidence that measured unrelated content. For a row whose `dependsOn` is not `tree`, green means NOT CURRENTLY REPRODUCIBLE and never FIXED. The repair is now on the trunk, so the row is ordinary history; the lesson is not, and it is the reason this field exists. The engineer's account of the defect: the test asserted `candidates equals sites flat`, which was stricter than the gate's own contract and demanded a cross-lane edit no run of this repository could make; the gate itself exits 0 with zero errors and downgrades the two unaccounted candidates to warnings because they are sections of `docs/agents/runner-facts.md`, which this seat owns.
repaired.staleWithinOneRun: Recorded because it is the point. This row read `repairedOnTrunk: null` and `AND #716 IS NOT MERGED` for the first forty minutes of the eighty-ninth window and was true when written. The engineer told this seat at 08:46Z that the test passes 19 of 19 at main's tip, which was also true and was about a different question. The merge landed at 09:25:25Z. A register entry about another seat's open row has a shelf life measured in minutes on this queue, so re-derive the row's state at the instant you publish, not at the instant you learn it.
repaired.repairedOnTrunkEvidence: gh pr view 716 --json mergeCommit -> fad56e1e; `git merge-base --is-ancestor fad56e1e origin/main` exits 0. The first draft of this field carried a sha this window had not resolved, which is the defect this evidence field exists to stop.

repaired.name: no source file outside a test orders timestamps as text
repaired.flipExpect: the offenders list is non-empty; the test prints each `<file>:<line> TEXTUAL_ORDER <text>` it found
repaired.note: The lint gate over the whole index, so ANY seat's commit can flip it, which is why `dependsOn` is repo-content and not tree. Three offenders on 613fc803. Two were real -- `r.ts > n.ts` and a descending `ts.localeCompare` in tools/seat/answered.mjs, a file that reads instants off both the board and the forge API, which is exactly the mixed-spelling case the lint exists for. The third was a FALSE POSITIVE in the lint itself: TIMESTAMP_NAME's `[Tt]s` alternative matched any identifier ending in those two letters, so `cmp.points < baseline.minPoints` -- two integers, in this tool -- read as a textual timestamp order. instant.mjs's own header already argues this case for `Date` (`update` and `candidate` end in it) and the rule had never been applied to `ts`.

repaired.resolvedNote: TWO SEATS WROTE THE SAME FIX INDEPENDENTLY, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW IS RESOLVED RATHER THAN DROPPED. This row's `repairPending` field said the repair was on this seat's 2026-11-08 branch and not yet on the trunk. That was true when written and it was already being overtaken: exo's 965a4554 landed at 23:32:29Z, eighteen minutes before this seat's f985dc02 at 23:50:06Z, and it narrowed the SAME alternative of TIMESTAMP_NAME and repaired the SAME two findings in tools/seat/answered.mjs. On 2026-11-09 the PM seat declined to merge the row by hand for that reason and handed it back. The settlement: exo's regex survives. The two patterns were checked for equivalence rather than compared by eye -- `Ts|\bts|_ts` against `Ts|_ts|\bts` over all 28,308 identifiers in this tree plus every string to four characters over the relevant alphabet, 157,672 strings, 0 disagreements -- so the code was the same fix twice and only the prose and the corpus differed. exo's prose carries the measurement (15,466 identifiers, 2.3 per cent accuracy on the `ts` tail) and the decision NOT to narrow `at`, and exo's corpus asserts the real `baseline.minPoints` line where this seat's interpolated a lowercase `minpoints`. A strictly weaker duplicate is not kept beside the thing it duplicates, so this seat's regex, prose and test were all dropped in the rebase and f985dc02 became empty.
repaired.notPaidByGreen: The `dependsOn: repo-content` caveat applies to this row and is NOT what cleared it. Green on a repo-content row means NOT CURRENTLY REPRODUCIBLE, never FIXED, because any seat's commit can flip it. What clears it here is a NAMED COMMIT on the trunk whose diff is the repair, verified by re-running the gate's own sweep at origin/main rather than by reading a colour off this tool. The rule is: a repo-content row is resolved by identifying the commit, not by observing the colour.
